title: All-hands DEI commitment Q&A (scratch)
content:
Purpose and context:
- Short note to self: this is a lightweight prep doc for the CEO + People Ops segment at the Mar 17 all-hands. Not the final script — collect feedback from Marta/Ezra and R&D leadership before locking.
- Goal: acknowledge progress, be transparent about gaps, announce two commitments (pilot mentoring circles + expanded parental leave policy) and field live Qs with clear follow-ups. Avoid legalese; be candid about where we still need work.

High-level talking points (rough order):
1) Why this matters now — one minute
   - We’re at 150+ teammates and growth is accelerating. Culture choices compound quickly.
   - Maintaining an inclusive environment is essential to build product responsibly and retain diverse talent.

2) What we’ve done — 90 seconds (brief wins, measurable):
   - Representation: hiring changes in 2025 increased underrepresented hires in Eng by 18% (ref: recruiting dashboard).
   - Manager training: launched inclusive feedback training pilot (20 managers) last quarter; NPS +20 among participants.
   - Pay equity review: completed company-wide review; adjustments applied in Q4 2025.

3) What we’re committing to today — 2 minutes (concrete, timebound):
   - Mentoring circles pilot: 6-month pilot starting April. Cross-functional groups of 6–8 with monthly facilitation. Goal: improve internal mobility and retention for early-career+underrepresented folks. Measure: participation, internal transfers, and retention delta.
   - Parental leave expansion: effective June 1, primary caregiver leave increases to 18 weeks (global policy to follow regionally). Hiring managers: we’ll add temporary coverage budget to avoid team burnout.

4) What we still need to improve — 60 seconds (honest):
   - Mid-level manager diversity still lags; pipeline work ongoing.
   - Employee resource groups underfunded vs. peers — commitment to allocate stable budget in Q2.

5) How we’ll measure progress — 45 seconds:
   - Quarterly DEI dashboard: hires by level, retention by cohort, manager demographics, program participation.
   - Publish a short (one pager) update after each quarter to the company.

6) Ask of the company — 30 seconds
   - Managers: encourage participation in mentoring circles and block 90 minutes/month for them.
   - ICs: volunteer as mentees or mentors; sign up form will go out after the all-hands.

7) Close: tone & CTA — 20 seconds
   - Gratitude for the work already done, recommitment to sustained effort, invite feedback via #peopleops-dei or the anonymous form.

Planned flow in all-hands (timing):
- CEO sets context (30s)
- Kira reads 2 commitments + metrics (2.5 min)
- Live Q&A (10 min) — moderated; take 3–4 live questions, then read top pre-submitted questions if time.
- Closing remark + link to sign-up form (15s)

Moderation notes (for moderator, likely Jonas):
- Use the queue in Slido (or use Zoom Q) and prioritize: a) clarifying Qs about policy mechanics; b) concerns about manager workload; c) questions about measurement/transparency.
- If a question touches legal/compensation specifics beyond scope, deflect: note we’ll follow up with the person privately and post anonymized response.

Pre-submitted Qs + suggested answers (editable):
Q1: How will the mentoring circles be staffed/facilitated?
A1: We’ll run 6-month cohorts with a trained facilitator (internal People Ops lead + rotational external coach for first cohort). Mentors come from cross-functional volunteers; we’ll recruit to ensure seniority mix. Budget for external facilitation is approved for the pilot.

Q2: Will the parental leave changes apply to contractors and international employees?
A2: Short answer: not immediately. We’re expanding the core full-time employee policy first globally where legal/benefits allow; contractors and region-specific variations handled on a case-by-case basis — People Ops will publish the regional note by May 1.

Q3: Does this affect compensation or promotion timelines?
A3: No changes to promotion criteria; however, we will train managers to account for equitable performance calibration, especially across leaves or reduced schedule transitions. Compensation review cycles remain the same.

Q4: How will you measure if mentoring circles actually help underrepresented groups?
A4: Primary metrics: retention (6/12 months), internal movement (transfers/promotion rates), and participant survey (psych safety, sponsorship access). We’ll share a mid-pilot snapshot at month 3 and a full evaluation after month 6.

Q5: Why is this happening now vs earlier?
A5: We reached the scale where small policy gaps produce outsized effects; we also had repeated feedback in last year’s engagement survey and exit interviews that pushed these items to the top. We should be proactive, not reactive.

Tougher live questions and suggested handling (tone guidance):
- Q: "How do I know this is more than PR?"
  Suggested response: "Fair question. I’ll be transparent: we’ve made progress but haven’t solved everything. Today’s moves are accompanied by measurable commitments and dedicated budget; we’ll publish quarterly results and invite external audit of certain metrics next year. If you want specifics on allocations, I’m happy to share the budget breakdown with leadership groups"'

- Q: "What happens if my manager says no to my participation?"
  Suggested: "Managers will be expected to support participation — we’re asking leads to block time. If someone is blocked, escalate to people_ops@redwood.ai; we’ll mediate and provide guidance to managers on prioritization"'

Open items / follow-ups before finalizing script:
- Confirm parental leave legal notes with legal (assigned: Marta) — due 2026-03-13.
- Final budget numbers for mentoring pilot (assigned: Ezra) — due 2026-03-12.
- Draft the 1-pager DEI dashboard template (assigned: Kira) — due 2026-03-20.
- Create sign-up Google form + opt-in privacy note (assign: Jonas) — due 2026-03-12.

Logistics & comms after all-hands:
- Send a summary email within 24 hours with links to sign-up, FAQ, and contact. Draft to be ready asap; planned owner: People Ops comms (Kira).
- Post anonymized Q&A doc to company Confluence page and link in #peopleops-dei.

Tone reminders for speaker(s):
- Use plain language; avoid jargon.
- Prioritize humility: name what we don’t know.
- Emphasize commitment to measurement and follow-through.

Potential PR sensitivity:
- Keep policy specifics and pay adjustments out of public external PR; this doc is for internal only. Legal review required before anything public-facing.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Consider asking 2 employees to share 30s anecdote in-person at all-hands — powerful but risk of singling out. If we do, get consent + prep them.
- Double-check time in agenda slot (10–12 mins total). If all-hands runs long, be ready to cut Q&A and post full responses.

End of draft — iterate with Marta/Ezra/Jonas.

Revision history (quick):
- 2026-02-28 initial outline
- 2026-03-02 added pre-submitted Qs
- 2026-03-11 updated pilot logistics and event_date
